title: Jupiter Doesn't Actually Orbit the Sun (Here's the Catch)

scenes.text: Jupiter doesn't orbit the Sun. Not exactly.
Two objects in space don't circle each other. They both circle a shared balance point, their centre of mass.
For Earth, that point sits deep inside the Sun, so the Sun barely moves. Jupiter is different.
Jupiter has two and a half times the mass of every other planet combined. Its balance point with the Sun lies just above the Sun's surface.
So the Sun and Jupiter both swing around a spot in empty space. The Sun wobbles.
That wobble is how we find planets around other stars. Watch a star shake, and you know something big is tugging on it. What else did your textbook get slightly wrong?

description:
Jupiter doesn't orbit the Sun. Not exactly.
Two bodies orbit their shared centre of mass, the barycentre. For Jupiter, which has about 2.5 times the mass of all the other planets combined, that point lies about 1.07 solar radii from the Sun's centre, just outside the Sun's surface. So the Sun and Jupiter both orbit a point in empty space, and the Sun wobbles. Astronomers use the same kind of wobble to discover planets around other stars.
What else do you think your textbook got slightly wrong?
